transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Nimbus EM), Diego Morales (Nimbus Backend), Sofia Alvarez (Nimbus Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm Maya from Redwood, this is Ravi, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Laura: Doing well, thanks. excited to see the SDK flow — we've skimmed the docs but want a hands-on walkthrough.
[00:12] Ravi: Great, today we'll do a quick overview of the python and typescript sdks, auth patterns, env setup, and then show the console and Optimize suggestions. we'll also touch on Dedicated and Private notes at the end.
[00:20] Diego: Sounds good. our main objective is to understand how long it takes to get a server-side integration up and running and what the auth and secrets surface looks like.
[00:30] Maya: Perfect. quick agenda: 1) pip/npm install, 2) env vars / api keys / sso, 3) quick code examples (python/ts), 4) running locally vs in prod, 5) console + optimize, 6) q&a and next steps.

--- Quickstarts / env setup ---
[02:05] Ravi: Alright let's start with python. pip install redwood-inference-sdk (note: that's the package name in the quickstart repo). then you set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, or you can use the SDK client to pass the key directly for short demos.
[02:23] Maya: for teams, we recommend using secrets manager and injecting at runtime, but for dev quickstarts env var is simplest.
[02:35] Diego: Is there SSO support for token issuance? we use SSO + automated provisioning.
[02:48] Ravi: Yes, for enterprise customers we integrate with SAML / oidc; the flow is via our control plane — you can mint short-lived instance tokens for the dataplane.There's a dedicated section in the security docs; i'll share the link.
[03:10] Sofia: And KMS? we need envelope encryption for model inputs stored in logs.
[03:18] Ravi: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). logs stored in the private deployment option can be encrypted with your KMS. for hosted infra we have BYOK patterns; again i'll attach the whitepaper.

[04:00] Ravi: Now a quick python snippet — i'll read it out so you can follow. from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-7b', prompt='Summarize customer order')
print(resp.text)
[04:20] Laura: what's the default timeout and retry policy in the SDK?
[04:26] Ravi: Default timeout is 30s for generation calls, with exponential backoff on 5xx. config is overridable at client init. we'll show the config object in the repo.

--- TypeScript quickstart ---
[07:10] Ravi: For TS: npm i @redwood/inference; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [...] });
[07:28] Diego: Do you support streaming responses in the TS SDK?
[07:33] Ravi: Yes, both python and ts support streaming via async iterators or event callbacks; browser and server semantics explained in the quickstart.

[08:00] Maya: i'll pause — any specific language or framework you plan to integrate with? i saw in your intake you use node microservices and python batch workers.
[08:10] Laura: Node for our API layer, python for offline enrichment. so we want both.

--- Auth patterns and envs ---
[09:20] Ravi: For auth patterns: short-lived tokens for server processes, per-route api keys for cost attribution, and service accounts for CI. For SSO we connect to your IdP and you can configure role-based grants.
[09:40] Maya: also note you can scope keys to models and routes to limit blast radius — helpful if you have public-facing endpoints.
[09:52] Sofia: audit logs — are token usages tied to user identities? we need per-request audit trails for compliance.
[10:00] Ravi: Yes, audit logs include token id, route, model, and originating IP. in Private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM.

--- Running locally vs prod ---
[11:30] Ravi: Running locally you can use the hosted API with local env vars or spin up a light docker dev image we provide. for prod we recommend either Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput or Private for VPC/air-gapped.
[11:47] Laura: How invasive is the Private install? our infra team prefers minimal changes.
[11:54] Ravi: Private is a control plane + dataplane package — installation is mostly k8s manifests or a guided AMI workflow. we provide an ops runbook. It's not trivial but we handle a lot of the heavy lifting with our deployment engineers.

--- Console walkthrough ---
[14:05] Maya: i'll share my screen — opening the Redwood Console. on the left you see models, routes, and Optimize suggestions.
[14:14] Ravi: The Optimize tab will suggest batching settings, quantization profiles, and cache TTLs based on observed traffic. for example, for short prompt families it recommended aggressive prefix caching to save tokens.
[14:35] Diego: do suggestions include expected cost delta?
[14:38] Maya: Yes, it shows estimated per-token cost and expected p95 latency change. you can simulate the delta on a sample traffic profile.

--- Demo: small code-to-console loop ---
[16:50] Ravi: i'm going to generate a couple of requests from the node sample app and show them hitting the console in real-time.
[17:05] (typing)
[17:20] Ravi: you can see the live trace, tokens, and latency per request. here's an example route configured with model redwood-chat-1, and you can bind it to a key with per-route quotas.
[17:40] Laura: Nice, how do we tag requests for cost allocation across product teams?
[17:46] Maya: you can use metadata headers (x-rw-team, x-rw-trace) and they appear in the cost breakdown and traces.

--- Optimize and batching notes ---
[19:30] Ravi: For throughput we recommend continuous batching on GPU-backed nodes. the Optimize profile suggested a batch size of 8 and a cache ttl of 30s for your prompt family. that reduced token charge estimate by ~22% in the sim.
[19:52] Diego: if we change models (7b -> 13b quantized) can Optimize simulate latency/cost tradeoffs?
[19:58] Ravi: Yes, it has model profiles — we maintain performance profiles per model and quantization variant, though numbers are approximations until we run on your exact infra.

--- Security / compliance ---
[22:10] Sofia: quick Q on data retention — what are defaults?
[22:15] Ravi: Default retention for hosted is 30 days for logs, with options to disable or export. Dedicated/Private give you full control. retention is configurable per-route in the Console.
[22:30] Sofia: And redaction?
[22:34] Ravi: You can enable automatic PII redaction for logged payloads, plus allow list/deny list patterns. We also support custom preprocess hooks.

--- POC / Benchmarking discussion ---
[25:00] Laura: For the POC we want a benchmark: 1k concurrent users hitting chat endpoints, p95 latency under 600ms for typical prompts. is that feasible?
[25:15] Ravi: With Dedicated GPU pools and optimized batching, that's achievable for smaller models (7b) — for chat with longer context and 13b it may be tougher. we should scope sample prompt sizes and dynamic concurrency.
[25:32] Maya: agreed — next step we'll collect sample prompts and SLOs and run a bench.

--- FAQs / common objections ---
[28:10] Diego: what's the billback model during POC? free credits or trial tier?
[28:18] Maya: we typically offer trial credits and usage-based billing during POC, and Reserved capacity proposals for Dedicated when you commit.
[28:26] Diego: any vendor lock-in for SDKs?
[28:31] Ravi: SDKs are thin wrappers over our REST endpoints; you can call the API directly. models are versioned and you can pin versions in config. no proprietary data format lock-in.

--- Live troubleshooting / dev questions ---
[32:00] (Diego shares screen)
[32:05] Diego: i'm trying the node sample and getting 401 sometimes.
[32:10] Maya: likely a key scope issue; are you rotating keys in your dev CI?
[32:12] Diego: we have a vault that rotates.
[32:15] Ravi: TTL on the dev token maybe too short; for testing use long-lived test key or configure service account tokens. Also check clock skew on your container — time drift can break token introspection.
[32:35] Diego: oh that's it, our test container had wrong timezone. fixed and calls are passing. thanks.

--- Wrap-up and next steps ---
[40:00] Maya: quick recap: we'll send the quickstart repo (python + ts samples), security docs (SOC2, KMS notes), and sample console screenshots; Ravi will help run the POC bench; Laura to share sample prompts and traffic profile.
[40:20] Laura: yes and i'll loop in infra for the Private install questions.
[40:30] Sofia: please include the KMS integration steps and audit log export options.
[40:36] Ravi: will do. i'll drop notes and links in the follow-up.

[41:00] Maya: any final Qs?
[41:05] Diego: not from me, looks solid.
[41:10] Laura: nope, thanks.
[41:15] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the repo and docs by Friday.
[41:25] (meeting ends)

Notes: references mentioned during call - quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart (sample link), security whitepaper link: https://redwood.ai/security (placeholder).
